subject: Archer: orphan evidence cleanup & canonicalization request
messages:
From: Tim D'Angelo <tim.dangelo@archersec.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Orphan evidence discovery for NovumCloud (Archer)

Hi Rafael,

Quick heads up from Archer's side: during a routine clean-up we discovered a number of "orphaned" evidence objects tied to the NovumCloud Archer profile. These appear to be remnants from a previous migration (mixed CAIQ/SIG import) and many lack canonical IDs / proof-of-possession metadata.

To avoid accidental deletion we're reaching out to confirm what Redwood wants retained vs. rehomed or removed. Attached is a small index we built (archer_orphan_index.csv) that lists keys, last-modified, size, and the profile path. Two quick questions for you:

- Do you want Archer to preserve these objects in a quarantine folder pending your review, or should we re-home them into your existing evidence buckets?
- For SOC 2 / CAIQ purposes, will Redwood provide a canonical mapping CSV (evidence ID -> CAIQ/SIG control) and SHA256 hashes, or do you prefer Archer to preserve originals for you to hash?

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week — we can share screen and step through the index.

Attachment: archer_orphan_index.csv (csv, ~120KB)

Thanks,

Tim D'Angelo
Integrator Relations, Archer Security
tim.dangelo@archersec.com
---
[Onboarding & integrations team]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Tim D'Angelo <tim.dangelo@archersec.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orphan evidence discovery for NovumCloud (Archer)

Tim — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV. We do not want any bulk deletions without an explicit Redwood sign-off.

High-level plan from our side:
1) Please preserve the objects in a quarantine path (do not delete).
2) We'll provide a canonicalization manifest that maps evidence -> CAIQ/SIG control and includes last-modified timestamps and SHA256 when available.
3) For items Redwood cannot prove possession of, we'll either (a) request re-upload/presign from Archer, or (b) mark as archival-exception depending on the control owner.

I've attached a short evidence_handback_template.csv and a soc2_evidence_guidance.md that explains the fields we need (canonical_id, control_tag, last_modified, sha256, uploader, original_path). Marissa will run the matching sweep; Irene will own CAIQ/SIG mapping.

Action items we need from Archer:
- Confirm quarantine path and retention SLA for quarantined objects.
- Re-send the index with object storage URLs and an example presign flow if re-home is required.
- If you can provide ETag/SHA256 in the index that helps expedite mapping.

We should probably do a quick 30-min sync. I can do Mon/Tue afternoon (PDT).

Attachment(s): evidence_handback_template.csv (csv, 4KB), soc2_evidence_guidance.md (md, 18KB)

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Thanks Rafael — we concur on quarantine. I've attached the full index (archer_orphan_index.csv) with an additional column for ETag where present and a short S3 listing sample for three keys.

A couple of clarifying notes:
- We can preserve quarantined objects for up to 90 days with an automatic snapshot; after that we'll start a retention purge unless we receive direction.
- Archer cannot compute SHA256 for objects on customer-managed S3 where we only have presigned GETs; if the bucket is Redwood-managed we can return hashes.

For the presign path, we're happy to: (a) take files into an Archer-managed preservation bucket, or (b) mark and generate presigned PUTs for your team to push re-homed files. Which is easiest for Redwood?

Attachment(s): archer_orphan_index.csv (csv, 214KB), s3_listing_sample.txt (txt, 12KB)

—Tim
